title.en: Cleft Sentences (It was Maria who …, What I need is …)
title.es: Las oraciones enfáticas (It was Maria who …, What I need is …)

text.en: A cleft sentence splits one sentence into two parts so that the important information stands apart. There are two main types. The it-cleft: “It was Maria who called the police.” The wh-cleft: “What I need is a long vacation.” The Spanish “Fue María quien llamó” and “Lo que necesito es…” match them, but English needs “it” as a dummy subject.
text.es: Una oración enfática divide una oración en dos partes para que la información importante quede aparte. Hay dos tipos principales. La it-cleft: «It was Maria who called the police.» La wh-cleft: «What I need is a long vacation.» El «Fue María quien llamó» y el «Lo que necesito es…» del español les corresponden, pero el inglés necesita «it» como sujeto formal.

rows: fue ayer cuando ocurrió (cosa, lugar o tiempo)

title.en: It-cleft: It + be + focus + that / who
title.es: It-cleft: It + be + foco + that / who

text.en: You can stress the subject, the object and an adverbial, not the verb. Who (or that) for people, that for things, places and times.
text.es: Se puede enfatizar el sujeto, el objeto y un adverbial, no el verbo. Who (o that) para personas, that para cosas, lugares y tiempos.

examples.es: It was Maria who called the police.

tr.en: It was Maria who called the police.
tr.es: Fue María quien llamó a la policía.

examples.es: It was in Paris that we first met.

tr.en: It was in Paris that we first met.
tr.es: Fue en París donde nos conocimos.

text.en: Negative and contrast: “It wasn’t the money that mattered.” “It was Tom, not Anna, who broke the vase.”
text.es: Negación y contraste: «It wasn’t the money that mattered.» «It was Tom, not Anna, who broke the vase.»

examples.es: It wasn't the money that mattered to her.

tr.en: It wasn't the money that mattered to her.
tr.es: No era el dinero lo que le importaba.

examples.es: It was Tom, not Anna, who broke the vase.

tr.en: It was Tom, not Anna, who broke the vase.
tr.es: Fue Tom, no Anna, quien rompió el florero.

text.en: The focus goes to the end of the sentence: “What I need is a long vacation.” The verb is was/is. After what … do, be is followed by the base verb: “What she did was call the police.”
text.es: El foco va al final de la oración: «What I need is a long vacation.» El verbo es was/is. Después de what … do, be va seguido del verbo base: «What she did was call the police.»

examples.es: What I need is a long vacation.

tr.en: What I need is a long vacation.
tr.es: Lo que necesito son unas vacaciones largas.

examples.es: What happened was that the car broke down.

tr.en: What happened was that the car broke down.
tr.es: Lo que pasó fue que el carro se descompuso.

title.en: All, the thing, the reason and the reverse form
title.es: All, the thing, the reason y la forma inversa

text.en: Instead of what you can use all, the thing (that), the reason (why): “All I want is a quiet life.” “The reason why I left is that the pay was low.” Reversed: “A quiet life is what I want.”
text.es: En lugar de what se puede usar all, the thing (that), the reason (why): «All I want is a quiet life.» «The reason why I left is that the pay was low.» A la inversa: «A quiet life is what I want.»

examples.es: All I want is a quiet life.

tr.en: All I want is a quiet life.
tr.es: Todo lo que quiero es una vida tranquila.

examples.es: A quiet life is what I want.

tr.en: A quiet life is what I want.
tr.es: Una vida tranquila es lo que quiero.

text.en: English needs “it” as the subject: not “Was Maria who called”, but “It was Maria who called”. A word-for-word copy of the Spanish “fue María quien” does not work without “it”.
text.es: El inglés necesita «it» como sujeto: no «Was Maria who called», sino «It was Maria who called». Una copia palabra por palabra del «fue María quien» no funciona sin «it».

text.en: In a wh-cleft it is “what”, not “that”: not “That I need is”, but “What I need is”. Was or is goes before the focus, and was after past events.
text.es: En la wh-cleft es «what», no «that»: no «That I need is», sino «What I need is». Antes del foco va was o is, y was después de hechos pasados.

speak.en: A cleft sentence splits one sentence into two parts so that the important information stands apart. The it-cleft: «It was Maria who called the police». Who, or that, for people, that for things, places and times. The wh-cleft: «What I need is a long vacation». After «what … do», «be» is followed by the base verb: «What she did was call the police». Instead of «what» you can use «all» and «the reason why»: «All I want is a quiet life». English needs «it» as the subject.
speak.es: Una oración enfática divide una oración en dos partes para que la información importante quede aparte. La it-cleft: «It was Maria who called the police». Who, o that, para personas, that para cosas, lugares y tiempos. La wh-cleft: «What I need is a long vacation». Después de «what … do», «be» va seguido del verbo base: «What she did was call the police». En lugar de «what» se puede usar «all» y «the reason why»: «All I want is a quiet life». El inglés necesita «it» como sujeto.

items.sentence: It was Maria ___ called the police.

why.en: For a person in the subject role: It was Maria who called.
why.es: Para una persona como sujeto: It was Maria who called.

what.en: What is not a relative pronoun for a person.
what.es: What no es un pronombre relativo para una persona.

whom.en: Whom is for an object; here Maria is the subject (she called).
whom.es: Whom es para un objeto; aquí Maria es el sujeto (ella llamó).

examples: It was Tom who left.
It was she who won.

tr.en: It was Maria who called the police.
tr.es: Fue María quien llamó a la policía.

items.sentence: It was in Paris ___ we first met.

why.en: For a place: It was in Paris that we met.
why.es: Para un lugar: It was in Paris that we met.

who.en: Who refers to people; Paris is a place.
who.es: Who se refiere a personas; Paris es un lugar.

what.en: What is not a relative pronoun in the it-cleft.
what.es: What no es un pronombre relativo en la it-cleft.

examples: It was here that it happened.
It was at home that we ate.

tr.en: It was in Paris that we first met.
tr.es: Fue en París donde nos conocimos por primera vez.

items.sentence: It was the noise ___ woke me up.

why.en: For a thing in the subject role: It was the noise that woke me.
why.es: Para una cosa como sujeto: It was the noise that woke me.

who.en: Who refers to people; noise is a thing.
who.es: Who se refiere a personas; el ruido es una cosa.

what.en: What is not a relative pronoun in the it-cleft.
what.es: What no es un pronombre relativo en la it-cleft.

examples: It was the rain that stopped us.
It was the heat that tired him.

tr.en: It was the noise that woke me up.
tr.es: Fue el ruido lo que me despertó.

items.sentence: ___ I need is a long vacation.

why.en: The wh-cleft: What I need is…
why.es: La wh-cleft: What I need is…

That.en: “That I need is” is not correct; the wh-cleft starts with what.
That.es: «That I need is» no es correcto; la wh-cleft empieza con what.

Which.en: “Which I need is” is not correct; the wh-cleft starts with what.
Which.es: «Which I need is» no es correcto; la wh-cleft empieza con what.

examples: What I want is peace.
What she needs is time.

tr.en: What I need is a long vacation.
tr.es: Lo que necesito es una vacación larga.

items.sentence: What happened ___ that the car broke down.

why.en: A past event: What happened was that…
why.es: Un hecho pasado: What happened was that…

were.en: Were is plural; what happened is singular.
were.es: Were es plural; what happened es singular.

has.en: “Has that” is not correct; the cleft needs the verb be (was).
has.es: «Has that» no es correcto; la cleft necesita el verbo be (was).

examples: What happened was simple.
What happened was that he left.

tr.en: What happened was that the car broke down.
tr.es: Lo que pasó fue que el carro se descompuso.

items.sentence: All I want ___ a quiet life.

why.en: All takes is in the cleft: All I want is…
why.es: All lleva is en la cleft: All I want is…

are.en: Are is plural; all I want is singular.
are.es: Are es plural; all I want es singular.

do.en: “Do a quiet life” is not correct; the cleft needs the verb be.
do.es: «Do a quiet life» no es correcto; la cleft necesita el verbo be.

examples: All I need is time.
All she wants is rest.

tr.en: All I want is a quiet life.
tr.es: Lo único que quiero es una vida tranquila.

items.sentence: What she did ___ call the police.

why.en: After what … did comes the verb be: What she did was call.
why.es: Después de what … did viene el verbo be: What she did was call.

has.en: “Has call” is not correct; after has a participle would be needed.
has.es: «Has call» no es correcto; después de has haría falta un participio.

did.en: “Did call” would be an emphatic form, but the cleft needs be.
did.es: «Did call» sería una forma enfática, pero la cleft necesita be.

examples: What he did was leave.
What they did was wait.

tr.en: What she did was call the police.
tr.es: Lo que ella hizo fue llamar a la policía.

items.sentence: The reason ___ I left is that the pay was low.

why.en: Stressing the reason: The reason why…
why.es: Destacar la razón: The reason why…

what.en: “The reason what” is not correct; you need why.
what.es: «The reason what» no es correcto; hace falta why.

who.en: Who refers to people; a reason is not a person.
who.es: Who se refiere a personas; una razón no es una persona.

examples: The reason why he came is simple.
The reason why she cried is clear.

tr.en: The reason why I left is that the pay was low.
tr.es: La razón por la que me fui es que la paga era baja.

items.sentence: It wasn't the money ___ mattered to her.

why.en: A negative cleft with a thing: It wasn’t the money that mattered.
why.es: Una cleft negativa con una cosa: It wasn’t the money that mattered.

who.en: Who refers to people; money is a thing.
who.es: Who se refiere a personas; el dinero es una cosa.

why.en: Why asks for a reason; here the money is the subject (it mattered).
why.es: Why pide una razón; aquí el dinero es el sujeto (importaba).

examples: It wasn't the price that worried me.
It wasn't the rain that stopped us.

tr.en: It wasn't the money that mattered to her.
tr.es: No era el dinero lo que le importaba a ella.

items.sentence: A quiet life is ___ I want.

why.en: The reversed wh-cleft: A quiet life is what I want.
why.es: La wh-cleft invertida: A quiet life is what I want.

that.en: “Is that I want” is not correct; the reversed cleft takes what.
that.es: «Is that I want» no es correcto; la cleft invertida lleva what.

which.en: “Is which I want” is not correct; the reversed cleft takes what.
which.es: «Is which I want» no es correcto; la cleft invertida lleva what.

examples: Peace is what we need.
Time is what she wants.

tr.en: A quiet life is what I want.
tr.es: Una vida tranquila es lo que quiero.

items.sentence: It is the cost ___ worries me.

why.en: For a thing in the subject role: It is the cost that worries me.
why.es: Para una cosa como sujeto: It is the cost that worries me.

what.en: What is not a relative pronoun in the it-cleft.
what.es: What no es un pronombre relativo en la it-cleft.

who.en: Who refers to people; cost is a thing.
who.es: Who se refiere a personas; el costo es una cosa.

examples: It is the time that matters.
It is the noise that bothers me.

tr.en: It is the cost that worries me.
tr.es: Es el costo lo que me preocupa.

why.en: An uncountable focus: What we need is more time.
why.es: Un foco incontable: What we need is more time.

are.en: Are is plural; more time is singular.
are.es: Are es plural; more time es singular.

have.en: “Have more time” is not correct; the cleft needs the verb be.
have.es: «Have more time» no es correcto; la cleft necesita el verbo be.

examples: What we need is help.
What I miss is sleep.

tr.en: What we need is more time.
tr.es: Lo que necesitamos es más tiempo.

items.sentence: It was yesterday ___ we got the news.

why.en: For a time: It was yesterday that we got the news.
why.es: Para un tiempo: It was yesterday that we got the news.

who.en: Who refers to people; yesterday is a time.
who.es: Who se refiere a personas; yesterday es un tiempo.

what.en: What is not a relative pronoun in the it-cleft.
what.es: What no es un pronombre relativo en la it-cleft.

examples: It was Monday that he left.
It was last year that it happened.

tr.en: It was yesterday that we got the news.
tr.es: Fue ayer cuando recibimos la noticia.

items.sentence: It was Tom, not Anna, ___ broke the vase.

why.en: For a person in the subject role: who.
why.es: Para una persona como sujeto: who.

whom.en: Whom is for an object; Tom is the subject (he broke it).
whom.es: Whom es para un objeto; Tom es el sujeto (él la rompió).

which.en: Which refers to things; Tom is a person.
which.es: Which se refiere a cosas; Tom es una persona.

examples: It was Eva, not Sam, who called.
It was he who asked.

tr.en: It was Tom, not Anna, who broke the vase.
tr.es: Fue Tom, no Anna, quien rompió el florero.

items.sentence: What I really enjoyed ___ the food.

why.en: The cleft verb in the past: What I enjoyed was the food.
why.es: El verbo de la cleft en pasado: What I enjoyed was the food.

were.en: Were is plural; food is singular.
were.es: Were es plural; food es singular.

did.en: “Did the food” is not correct; the cleft needs the verb be.
did.es: «Did the food» no es correcto; la cleft necesita el verbo be.

examples: What I liked was the view.
What I loved was the music.

tr.en: What I really enjoyed was the food.
tr.es: Lo que realmente disfruté fue la comida.

items.sentence: The thing ___ annoys me is the noise.

why.en: After the thing comes that: The thing that annoys me.
why.es: Después de the thing va that: The thing that annoys me.

who.en: Who refers to people; a thing is not a person.
who.es: Who se refiere a personas; una cosa no es una persona.

what.en: “The thing what” is not correct; you need that.
what.es: «The thing what» no es correcto; hace falta that.

examples: The thing that worries me is time.
The thing that helps is rest.

tr.en: The thing that annoys me is the noise.
tr.es: Lo que me molesta es el ruido.

items.sentence: What he did was ___ the window.

why.en: After what … did, be is followed by the base verb: What he did was break.
why.es: Después de what … did, be va seguido del verbo base: What he did was break.

broke.en: “Was broke” is not correct; after was comes the base verb here.
broke.es: «Was broke» no es correcto; después de was va el verbo base aquí.

broken.en: “Was broken” would be a passive; here you need the base form of the active verb.
broken.es: «Was broken» sería una pasiva; aquí hace falta la forma base del verbo activo.

examples: What he did was leave.
What she did was run.

tr.en: What he did was break the window.
tr.es: Lo que hizo fue romper la ventana.
